Different tasks get different models, chosen for cost and quality tradeoffs: Task Model Output Why SOAP/DAP note drafts Claude Sonnet (latest) SSE streaming text Best nuanced clinical writing, strong instruction following, streams reliably Session prep brief GPT-4o JSON (structured) Reliable enforced JSON via response_format , fast response Homework suggestions GPT-4o JSON (structured) Structured JSON, creative but grounded, good at modality-specific thinking Patient summary refresh Claude Haiku (latest) Plain text Fast, low-cost, excellent summarization — runs after every finalized note Note embeddings text-embedding-3-small vector(1536) $0.02/1M tokens, 1536 dimensions, excellent semantic quality Search query embedding text-embedding-3-small vector(1536) Same model as note embeddings — consistent embedding space required ℹ Model versioning Model IDs are configured in environment variables ( ANTHROPIC_MODEL , OPENAI_MODEL ). Never hardcode model IDs in business logic. When a new Claude or GPT version releases, update the env var and test before deploying — model behavior can change between versions.

Every AI call starts by assembling a PatientContext object. This is the most important function in the codebase — what goes in determines what comes out. Context piece Max tokens Strategy Why this limit System prompt ~500 Fixed per task type Constant — doesn't scale with patient history Patient profile + concerns + diagnoses ~200 Always included in full Small, high-value — always needed Rolling AI summary ~300 Always included in full This IS the memory layer — never truncate it Active treatment goals ~200 All active goals included Goals shape every clinical decision — always include Last 3–5 session notes ~2,000 400 tokens per note max Recency is more valuable than completeness Recent homework (last 3) ~200 Title + status only Low-token, high-relevance for continuity Therapist raw notes (this session) ~2,000 Included in full This is the primary signal — never truncate Total ~5,400 Well within Claude's 200k and GPT-4o's 128k limits The budget is conservative by design. Claude Sonnet supports 200k tokens — we use 5k. The reason: prompt caching. Anthropic's prompt cache TTL means frequently-used patient summaries and static system prompts are cached and not re-billed. Keeping prompts short and stable maximizes cache hit rate.

Used for: POST /ai/prep/:sessionId . Model: GPT-4o with response_format: { type: "json_object" } . You are an AI assistant helping a licensed {modality} therapist prepare for a session. You are NOT a therapist. You are a preparation tool only. Never diagnose. Never prescribe. Never make clinical decisions. THERAPIST CONTEXT: Modality: {modality} | License type: {licenseType} PATIENT: {firstName} | Session # {sessionNumber} Primary concerns: {concerns} Active diagnoses (context only, do not reference in output): {diagnoses} ROLLING AI SUMMARY (what the AI understands about this patient so far): {aiSummary} ACTIVE TREATMENT GOALS: {goals} LAST {n} SESSIONS (newest first, context for continuity): {recentSessionNotes} LAST ASSIGNED HOMEWORK: Title: {hwTitle} | Status: {hwStatus} | Category: {hwCategory} Generate a concise session preparation brief for the therapist to read in 90 seconds. Return EXACTLY this JSON structure (no other text): { "recap": "2-3 sentence summary of what happened last session and key themes. Write as if briefing a colleague.", "suggestedQuestions": ["Question 1", "Question 2", "Question 3", "Question 4"], "homeworkFollowUp": "One sentence on how to approach checking in on the homework assignment.", "patterns": "One sentence describing a notable cross-session pattern, or null if none is evident." } RULES: - Questions MUST match the therapist's modality (CBT questions for CBT, psychodynamic for psychodynamic, etc.) - Be concise — therapist reads this in 90 seconds before walking into the room - If information is missing or this is session 1, say so clear

Used for: POST /ai/note/draft (format=SOAP). Model: Claude Sonnet, SSE streaming. You are an AI assistant helping a licensed therapist draft a SOAP progress note. This is a DRAFT for therapist review and editing. It is NOT a final clinical document. The therapist will review, edit, and finalize before it becomes part of the record. PATIENT: {firstName} | Session # {sessionNumber} | {date} MODALITY: {modality} PRIMARY CONCERNS: {concerns} PATIENT CONTEXT (recent history — use for continuity, not verbatim copying): Rolling summary: {aiSummary} Last sessions (for continuity): {recentSessionNotes} Active goals: {goals} Homework status: {homeworkStatus} THERAPIST'S RAW NOTES FROM THIS SESSION (primary source — trust this above all else): --- {rawNotes} --- Draft a professional SOAP progress note based ONLY on the therapist's raw notes above. The context sections are for continuity — do not add details from prior sessions unless directly relevant to what the therapist noted today. SOAP FORMAT DEFINITIONS: - Subjective: What the patient reported — their words, feelings, experiences - Objective: Therapist's direct observations — affect, presentation, engagement, behavior - Assessment: Clinical synthesis — themes, progress toward goals, session arc - Plan: Next steps — homework, next session focus, any referrals or follow-up STRICT RULES: 1. Use ONLY information present in the therapist's raw notes 2. If a field cannot be written from the raw notes, write "[Therapist to complete]" 3. Do not fabricate quotes, events, clinical observations, or patient statements 4. Keep each section

Used for: POST /ai/note/draft (format=DAP). Model: Claude Sonnet, SSE streaming. You are an AI assistant helping a licensed therapist draft a DAP progress note. This is a DRAFT for therapist review. Not a final clinical document. PATIENT: {firstName} | Session # {sessionNumber} | {date} MODALITY: {modality} | CONCERNS: {concerns} CONTEXT (for continuity): {context} THERAPIST'S RAW NOTES: --- {rawNotes} --- DAP FORMAT DEFINITIONS: - Data: Observable information — what was reported, what was observed, events discussed - Assessment: Clinical interpretation — what the data means for the treatment arc - Plan: Concrete next steps RULES: Same as SOAP — use only raw notes, no fabrication, write "[Therapist to complete]" for gaps. Used for: POST /ai/homework/suggest . Model: GPT-4o with JSON mode. You are helping a {modality} therapist generate homework assignments for a patient. You are a tool — not a therapist. The therapist selects and approves all homework. PATIENT: {firstName} THERAPEUTIC MODALITY: {modality} PRIMARY CONCERNS: {concerns} TODAY'S SESSION THEMES (from therapist's raw notes): {sessionThemes} ACTIVE TREATMENT GOALS: {goals} PREVIOUSLY ASSIGNED HOMEWORK (for variety — avoid repeating recent assignments): {previousHomework} Generate 3 distinct homework options. Each must be: - Concrete and immediately actionable by the patient - Appropriate to the stated therapeutic modality - Grounded in today's session themes - Different in category from the other two options Return EXACTLY this JSON (no other text): { "options": [ { "title": "Short name for the assignment (5-8 words)", "description": "Detailed patient-facing instructions — what to do, when, how often. 3-5 sentences.", "category": "journaling|behavioral|exposure|mindfulness|social|psychoeducation", "rationale": "One sentence explaining why this fits the session themes and modality." }, { ... }, { ... } ] } RULES: - Do not suggest medication, diagnosis, or clinical interventions requiring a license - Homework must be completable independently by the patient between sessions - Exposure homework should be graduated — never jump to the feared stimulus directly - CBT: favor thought records, behavioral experiments, activity scheduling - DBT: favor diary cards, skills practice, chain analysis - Psychodynamic: favor journaling, dream logs,

Used by: refresh-summary BullMQ job (after every note finalization). Model: Claude Haiku. You are updating a rolling clinical summary for a therapist's internal reference. This summary helps the AI prepare better session briefs and note drafts. It is NOT part of the official clinical record — it is a tool for the AI, reviewed by the therapist. PATIENT: {firstName} | Total sessions completed: {sessionCount} PREVIOUS SUMMARY (written after session {prevSessionNum} ): {previousSummary} NEWEST FINALIZED SESSION NOTE (Session # {sessionNumber} , {date} ): {latestNote} Update the summary to reflect the newest session. The summary should capture the patient's overall treatment arc — not just the latest session. REQUIREMENTS: - 3-5 sentences maximum - Focus on: what has improved, what persists, recent breakthroughs or patterns, current clinical picture - Written for a therapist who knows this patient — not an external reader - Clinically accurate but not diagnostic — no DSM codes or diagnoses - If this is session 1, summarize the presenting picture only Return ONLY the updated summary text. No JSON wrapper. No preamble. No "Here is the summary:"

Tier 1 — Redis What: Active session state. Session prep brief (cached 24h). In-progress note draft. Rate limit counters. TTL: 24 hours for prep cache. Session-scoped for note drafts. Used for: Zero-latency reads during live sessions. Not the source of truth — PostgreSQL is. Tier 2 — PostgreSQL What: Rolling 3–5 sentence AI summary per patient. Stored in Patient.aiSummary . Update: After every note finalization, via refresh-summary BullMQ job. Used for: Injected into every AI call — session prep, note draft, homework. The "working memory" of the system. Tier 3 — pgvector What: Every finalized note embedded as a 1536-dimensional vector. Stored in NoteEmbedding . Update: After every note finalization, via embed-note BullMQ job. Used for: Natural language search. Deep context retrieval for complex queries.

// apps/api/src/jobs/embed-note.job.ts async processEmbedNote(job: Job<{ noteId: string }>) { const note = await this.prisma.sessionNote.findUniqueOrThrow({ where: { id: job.data.noteId }, include: { session: true } }) // Build text to embed — include all populated note fields const noteText = [ note.subjective && `Subjective: ${note.subjective}`, note.objective && `Objective: ${note.objective}`, note.assessment && `Assessment: ${note.assessment}`, note.plan && `Plan: ${note.plan}`, note.data && `Data: ${note.data}`, note.dapAssessment && `Assessment: ${note.dapAssessment}`, note.dapPlan && `Plan: ${note.dapPlan}`, note.freeText && note.freeText, ].filter(Boolean).join('\n') // Get embedding from OpenAI const response = await this.openai.embeddings.create({ model: 'text-embedding-3-small', input: noteText, }) const vector = response.data[0].embedding // float[1536] // Upsert — handles re-embedding if note is edited after initial embedding await this.prisma.$executeRaw` INSERT INTO "NoteEmbedding" (id, "noteId", "patientId", "therapistId", content, embedding, "createdAt") VALUES (${cuid()}, ${note.id}, ${note.session.patientId}, ${note.session.therapistId}, ${noteText}, ${vector}::vector, NOW()) ON CONFLICT ("noteId") DO UPDATE SET content = EXCLUDED.content, embedding = EXCLUDED.embedding ` }

These rules are enforced at the prompt level, not in application code. Every prompt template includes them. They cannot be overridden by user input. Rule Prompt enforcement Consequence if violated Never diagnose "Never diagnose. No DSM codes in outputs." Clinical liability. Therapist edits the note regardless. Never fabricate "Use ONLY information from raw notes. Missing = [Therapist to complete]." False clinical record. This is the highest-risk failure mode. Always a draft System prompt labels all output as "DRAFT for review" False sense of authority. UI reinforces this with ✦ badge. No medication "Do not suggest medication or prescriptions" Out of scope. Regulatory risk. Modality-aware Therapist modality injected in every prompt Irrelevant or wrong suggestions. Risk nudge only Separate application-layer check, not in prompt See below — soft nudge, never a clinical alarm.

The risk nudge is NOT done by AI prompt — it's done by a keyword pattern match in the application layer, applied to finalized note text before the response is sent to the client. If specific terms are detected (suicidal ideation, homicidal ideation, self-harm, specific plan or means references), a soft callout is returned alongside the note: // apps/api/src/notes/notes.service.ts (post-finalization check) const RISK_PATTERNS = [ /suicid/i, /self.harm/i, /hurt.*self/i, /homicid/i, /want to die/i, /end.*(my|their|his|her) life/i, /specific plan/i, /means.*access/i, ] function checkRiskPatterns(noteText: string): boolean { return RISK_PATTERNS.some(pattern => pattern.test(noteText)) } // If true, the API response includes: // "riskNudge": "This note may contain content warranting a safety assessment review." // This is displayed as a soft callout in the UI — not an alarm, not required action. The nudge is informational only. It does not block finalization, does not send any alert, and does not create a mandatory action. The therapist is a licensed professional who has already read and edited this note — the nudge is a safety net, not a clinical decision.

AI calls can fail for several reasons. The system handles each gracefully: Error type Behavior User sees AI provider 5xx (outage) BullMQ retries 3x with exponential backoff "Generation failed. Try again." Raw notes are saved. Rate limit (provider 429) Retry after Retry-After header Brief delay, then auto-retry Invalid JSON from model Retry once with "return valid JSON" emphasis Transparent to user if retry succeeds JSON retry also fails Return error to client "Generation failed. Try again." Raw notes saved. Context too large (edge case) Truncate oldest session notes first Note quality may be lower — not shown to user Network timeout SSE stream closes, client detects disconnect "Connection lost. Retry generation." ✓ Raw notes are always saved first Before any AI call, the therapist's raw notes are saved to the database. If AI generation fails entirely, the therapist still has their raw notes. They can try again, or use the raw notes as the basis for a manual note. AI failure is never data loss.

Role first, scope second, rules last. Every prompt starts with the AI's role and what it is NOT. Then defines the task. Rules come at the end where they're most recently primed. Explicit format enforcement. JSON output prompts always specify the exact structure, field names, and types. Ambiguity in format = inconsistent parsing = user-facing bugs. Placeholder naming. All dynamic values use {camelCase} placeholders that match the PatientContext field names. No magic strings. Modality injection. The therapist's modality is injected into every prompt. CBT therapists get CBT-appropriate questions and homework. This is not optional — it's the core value differentiation. No hallucination escape hatch. The prompt explicitly defines what happens when information is missing: write "[Therapist to complete]". There is no room for the model to be helpful by guessing. Test prompts with adversarial inputs. Before deploying a prompt change, test it with raw notes that are: very short (2 words), very long (1000 words), first session (no prior context), and emotionally intense (crisis content). The prompt must handle all gracefully. ← Previous API Reference Back to → Overview

The NestJS API is a single deployable unit. AI processing, search, and CRUD are all in one service. The benefit: simpler debugging, shared transactions, one deployment target. Extract the AI module into a separate service only when you need independent scaling — typically at ~10,000 active users where AI inference is the bottleneck. The NestJS module boundary makes this extraction clean.

Pinecone adds infrastructure complexity (another service to manage, another cost center) and an extra network hop. pgvector in PostgreSQL handles millions of embeddings efficiently with HNSW indexing, with the added benefit that row-level therapist isolation is enforced at the database layer. Migration trigger: If note embedding count exceeds 500k, or if metadata filtering requirements become complex enough that raw pgvector queries are difficult to maintain, migrate to Pinecone. The search/ NestJS module is the only code that changes.

h: 3. SSE Over WebSockets for AI Streaming
x: AI note generation streams token-by-token to the frontend using Server-Sent Events. SSE is simpler than WebSockets for one-directional streaming (server → client), works through HTTP/2 without special infrastructure, and requires no WebSocket server management. The frontend uses a custom useAiStream hook that manages the EventSource lifecycle, error handling, and reconnection. When the stream ends, the full JSON note object is returned in the final event.

Note generation itself streams directly. But the post-finalization memory pipeline (embedding and summary refresh) runs entirely via BullMQ jobs. Benefits: the therapist sees "Finalized" immediately, jobs are retried on failure, job history is inspectable. Two queues: note-embeddings and patient-summaries . Both use Redis as the queue backend. Summary refresh is chained to fire after embedding completes (not in parallel) to ensure the embedding is available when the summary is generated.

h: 5. Row-Level Therapist Isolation in Every Query
x: Every Prisma query that touches a Patient, Session, Note, Goal, or Homework record filters by therapistId = authenticatedUserId . This is enforced in the service layer — not just the controller layer — to prevent accidental cross-therapist data exposure. Automated tests verify that therapist A cannot access therapist B's data even with a valid JWT.

The product An AI documentation and patient-memory tool for independent therapists. It sits beside the therapist's EHR and does not record sessions. The build Turborepo monorepo: NestJS API, Next.js app, Prisma on Postgres with pgvector. 38 TypeScript files, about 5,700 lines, 9 commits over 4 days (21–24 Jul 2026). The state Core loop works locally: patient → session → raw notes → AI draft → edit → finalize → memory. Production login, compliance and billing are not built.

Independent therapists run a one-person clinical practice. After each session they write a progress note, and before the next one they try to remember what happened weeks ago. The tools they use were built for billing, not for clinical continuity: an EHR stores notes but does not help recall them, and a blank SOAP template starts from zero every time. AI scribes now address the writing half. APA's 2025 survey shows the share of psychologists who have never used AI at work fell from 71% to 44% in a year, and use is mostly administrative ( Research §3 ). But most of those tools want to record the session , which raises consent, retention and psychotherapy-notes questions that many clinicians are uncomfortable with. About nine in ten psychologists report concerns about AI. The gap we chose: notes and memory for the therapist who does not want a recording tool in the room.

Segment Why Open questions Primary: US solo therapists (LCSW, LMFT, LPC, PsyD) in private practice Own the buying decision, feel the paperwork directly, talk to each other in dense communities Typical raw-note habits; how much they will type versus dictate Secondary: 2–10 therapist clinics where the owner also sees clients Higher revenue per account; needs roles and admin views Whether owners want visibility into notes (a privacy red line) Later: Indian clinicians Large, underserved; Razorpay/UPI billing Lower willingness to pay; "counsellor" is an unregulated title ( Research §6 )

The original plan assumed a feature gap: "no competitor combines AI notes, session prep and cross-session memory." A competitor review in October 2026 found that was wrong . Upheal, Mentalyc and SimplePractice all advertise cross-session features. Pricing was also off: Eleos is an enterprise product, not a $200 solo plan, and TherapyNotes and Upheal cost more or less than we had written. Two things survived scrutiny and now carry the strategy: Text-first. No audio is recorded. That avoids recording consent, transcript retention and most of the psychotherapy-notes ambiguity, and it is a clear trust story in a market where SimplePractice began defaulting new users into de-identified transcript retention in June 2026. EHR-agnostic memory. Competitor AI that ships inside an EHR is locked to it. A therapist who already uses SimplePractice or TherapyNotes can add TherapOS with no migration. The full evidence, with confidence tags, is on the Research page .

Before a session the therapist opens a prep brief built from goals, the last five completed sessions (note text truncated to a token budget), and recent homework: key topics, interventions to consider, goals to review, and homework to follow up.
During or after the session they type raw notes into the session page. Nothing is recorded.

The draft endpoint streams a structured note in the chosen format. The system prompt forbids fabrication and diagnosis, requires "[Therapist to complete]" for gaps, and uses neutral third-person clinical language.
The therapist edits every field and finalizes. Finalized notes cannot be edited.
Finalizing queues a background job: embed the note into pgvector, then regenerate the patient's rolling summary from the last ten finalized notes. The next prep brief starts from that memory.

h: Versus existing tools and the evidence

We found no public description of an activity drafted from this client's documented plan, approved by the clinician, with patient reflections flowing back into the next prep brief ( Inferred , marketing pages only; Blueprint is the nearest). Evidence for homework is correlational : Kazantzis 2016 (17 studies, N=2,312) finds g≈0.79 association between CBT homework compliance and outcomes, but assigning homework is not shown to cause it, and self-reported compliance gives weaker effects. Could it differentiate more than documentation? Probably, because it is harder to copy and creates daily patient-side usage that raises retention. But it also adds PHI surface, regulatory exposure and a second user type. Verdict: a gated pilot, not an MVP feature.

A Session is the scheduled meeting event — date, duration, type (Individual / Couples / Family / Group), and status (Scheduled / In Progress / Completed / Cancelled). A Session Note is the clinical documentation attached to that session. One session has exactly one note. The note lifecycle: therapist inputs raw notes → AI generates a structured draft → therapist edits → therapist finalizes. Finalization triggers the async memory pipeline.

When a note is finalized, two BullMQ background jobs fire automatically: embed-note — converts the finalized note to a 1,536-dimensional vector using OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small and stores it in NoteEmbedding . Powers natural language search. refresh-summary — calls Claude Haiku with the last 3 finalized notes plus the existing summary, and generates a new 3–5 sentence patient summary. Stored in Patient.aiSummary . Injected into all subsequent AI calls for this patient. Both jobs are async. The therapist sees the note as finalized immediately. Memory updates complete in 10–30 seconds in the background.

TherapOS is the AI-native operating system for independent therapists. It is not an EHR. It is not a therapy app. It is not another AI chatbot companion. The aspiration is an AI copilot a therapist opens before every session; that it becomes something they cannot practice without is a hypothesis, not a validated outcome. The product handles the clinical workflow that happens around therapy sessions: preparation, documentation, memory, and search. The AI remembers everything, prepares everything, and handles the busywork. The therapist remains completely in control. The 10-year vision: Every session makes the AI smarter about that patient. After 20 sessions, TherapOS understands the treatment arc better than any EHR ever could. Eventually, the question is not "can a therapist use TherapOS?" — it is "can a therapist practice as well without it?" The answer becomes no. That is the product goal: not lock-in through friction, but lock-in through indispensability.

They don't have to switch anything. TherapOS explicitly excludes billing, scheduling, and insurance. The pitch: "Keep SimplePractice for billing. Use TherapOS for everything clinical." Compound memory (hypothesis): Every finalized note deepens the patient summary. Competitors also advertise cross-session features, so memory alone is not a moat. The memory system is the structural moat. Three tiers, each serving a different purpose: Tier 1 — Redis Active session state. Session prep brief cache (24h TTL). In-progress note draft. Fast reads during live sessions. No persistence beyond TTL. Tier 2 — PostgreSQL Rolling AI patient summary (3–5 sentences). Updated after every finalized note via BullMQ job. Injected into every AI call for this patient. Tier 3 — pgvector Every finalized note embedded (text-embedding-3-small, 1536d). Searched via cosine similarity for NL search. Permanent — enables recall of any session content.

pgvector with HNSW indexing was chosen over Pinecone for the MVP. Reasons: no extra infrastructure, cost efficiency at scale below 500k embeddings, and PostgreSQL's row-level security means therapist data isolation is enforced at the index level without additional middleware. Migration path: if vector count exceeds 500k or metadata filtering complexity outgrows pgvector, migrate to Pinecone. This is a single-service change — the rest of the system doesn't need to change.

Authentication via Clerk. No custom auth — Clerk handles session management, MFA, OAuth (Google, Apple), and device trust. Clerk webhooks sync user creation/deletion events to the TherapOS User table. The ClerkGuard NestJS guard verifies the JWT on every API call and extracts the therapist ID for row-level isolation.

HIPAA gives "psychotherapy notes" (45 CFR 164.501) extra protection when kept separate from the record. TherapOS finalized notes are progress notes in the record. Raw session notes the therapist types are the closest analogue to process notes, so they are treated as the most sensitive data: excluded from analytics, optionally kept off the AI path, and never shared across clinic accounts. Counsel must confirm this design.

Illinois (HB 1806, 2025) restricts AI from independent therapeutic decisions, unreviewed treatment plans and emotion or mental-state detection, while allowing administrative support. Nevada (AB 406) and others restrict AI-delivered care; Utah regulates mental-health chatbots. TherapOS is documentation software with mandatory therapist review, but features such as risk flags, mood inference and AI-suggested interventions need legal review per state before launch. Trackers disagree on 2026 additions, so verify against statutes.

Text-first design avoids audio recording and therefore APA Standard 4.03 recording consent. Therapists should still disclose AI use to clients; TherapOS will provide a disclosure template naming the tool and its vendors.

TherapOS is documentation software. It assists with note-writing — it does not make clinical decisions, does not produce diagnoses, and does not prescribe or recommend treatment. This places TherapOS outside FDA Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) Class II/III as long as we maintain this scope. Adding risk-scoring features that make specific clinical recommendations (e.g., "Patient has elevated suicide risk — recommend hospitalization") would require regulatory review. We have a policy commitment to consult a regulatory attorney before shipping any such feature.

The DPDP Rules were notified on 13 November 2025. Consent-manager provisions apply from 13 November 2026 and most substantive duties from about 13 May 2027. Our plan, subject to legal confirmation: Treat health data as high-risk regardless of statutory category. (To our reading the Act has no separate "sensitive personal data" class, although practitioner guides say otherwise; the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 also applies to consent.) Host Indian accounts in an Indian region where feasible; assess cross-border transfer rules before sending any data to US AI vendors. Explicit, granular consent and a Data Protection Officer or contact as the Rules require once applicable. RCI (CRR) registration is mandatory only for clinical and rehabilitation psychologists; counsellors have no regulated title, so the India ICP needs defining.

These rules are baked into every prompt template and cannot be overridden by user input: Always a draft. Every AI output is explicitly labeled as a draft. Finalizing requires a deliberate therapist action. Never fabricate. If information is missing, write "[Therapist to complete]" — never invent clinical details, quotes, or observations. No diagnosis. No DSM codes, no clinical diagnoses in any AI outputs. Prompts explicitly prohibit this. Editable at every step. Every AI-generated field is a plain text editor. The therapist can delete the entire draft. Transparent. All AI content shows a ✦ AI indicator. Audit log records AI generation events separately from therapist edits. Risk nudge — deferred. A soft "may warrant a safety review" prompt was previously planned for the MVP. It is now on hold pending legal review, because some state laws restrict AI mental-state detection and a false negative creates a false sense of safety. If shipped, it will be therapist-configurable, never a diagnosis, never a required action. Modality-aware. Suggested questions and homework always respect the therapist's stated therapeutic modality.

x: Search only works on finalized notes (they need to be embedded first). If you finalized a note less than 60 seconds ago, wait for the embedding job to complete. You can check embedding status in Settings → Data.

h: HIPAA: psychotherapy notes versus progress notes
x: Under 45 CFR 164.501 , psychotherapy notes are a mental-health professional's notes documenting or analysing the content of a counselling session, kept separate from the rest of the record . They get extra protection and generally need specific authorisation to disclose. The definition excludes medication monitoring, session times, modalities and frequencies, test results, and summaries of diagnosis, functional status, treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis and progress. Verified for the definition; Reported for how it applies to AI output — we found no authoritative guidance. ✦ Product implication TherapOS finalized notes are progress notes (part of the record). Raw session notes the therapist types are closer to process / psychotherapy notes . Design rule: raw notes are treated as the most sensitive data, stay out of analytics and embeddings by default, and the therapist can choose to keep them off the AI path entirely. This is a Phase-1 requirement, not an afterthought. Get counsel to confirm the classification.
